discovery: Twistronics: prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics - two-dimensional quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero's group (Nature 2018, two papers) realised this with exquisitely controlled tear-and-stack devices, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity tunable by a simple gate voltage. This established the twist angle as a new, continuously adjustable parameter of matter and created the field of moire quantum materials. Within a few years, the platform yielded orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, strange-metal transport and, in twisted MoTe2 and rhombohedral graphene, fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. Laboratories worldwide, including many outside the traditional centres, now use van der Waals moire devices to study strongly correlated and topological electrons. The work pairs a clear theoretical prediction with rigorous experimental discovery, and it has changed how condensed-matter physics is done.
